title: Robust Hamiltonian engineering with subensemble control
authors: Wenjie Gong, Matteo Votto, Soonwon Choi
abstract: We present a robust protocol to reshape interactions in a spin ensemble based on global control pulse sequences applied to multiple subensembles in parallel. This setting arises naturally from ensembles of solid-state defects or multi-species atomic arrays. We show that it is provably computationally hard to find pulse sequences that simultaneously engineer interactions both within and between subensembles. Despite its formal hardness, we identify a set of necessary or sufficient conditions under which one can synthesize a target Hamiltonian from the native one. Moreover, we introduce efficient numerical strategies for designing pulse sequences that engineer target Hamiltonians robust against common control imperfections. As a specific application, we discuss the robust generation of two-mode spin squeezing in dual-species atomic ensembles, which is a challenging task without subensemble control. Our results provide a practical toolbox to design novel quantum simulation and sensing experiments with minimal control overhead.
summary: This paper develops a robust protocol for engineering desired interactions in multi-subensemble quantum systems, such as atomic arrays. It tackles the theoretical difficulty of Hamiltonian control by providing necessary and sufficient conditions and efficient numerical design strategies. The results demonstrate that these robust sequences can successfully generate quantum states, like spin-squeezed states, even when subjected to realistic experimental control errors.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of robustly engineering target interactions (Hamiltonians) in multi-subensemble quantum systems using global control pulse sequences.
main_result: They provide a practical toolbox showing that target Hamiltonians can be engineered robustly against common control imperfections (Amplitude, Frequency, Pulse-Width errors) in systems like atomic ensembles.
method: The methodology combines theoretical analysis of Hamiltonian engineering (using Floquet-Magnus expansion and completeness conditions) with numerical optimization techniques to design error-mitigating pulse sequences.
model_or_system: The work applies to spin ensembles, modeled using generalized Gell-Mann operators, arising naturally in solid-state defects or multi-species atomic arrays. Specific applications include dual-species atomic ensembles and Rydberg atom arrays.
key_observables: Two-mode spin squeezing parameter ($\xi$), and the achievable effective Hamiltonian ($	ilde{H}$).
important_parameters: Error strengths ($\epsilon, \delta$), number of subensembles ($n$), and the length/design of the pulse sequence (e.g., unitary 4-design).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the completeness of toggling-frame unitaries forming a unitary 4-design to ensure full control over the interaction space.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison of spin squeezing achieved using bare vs. robust pulse sequences for both optical cavity and Rydberg atom settings under varying error strengths.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the general theory of Hamiltonian engineering and its computational hardness, to deriving necessary and sufficient conditions, and finally demonstrating robust implementation and application in specific atomic platforms.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides concrete, robust protocols for controlling complex many-body interactions in atomic systems, moving beyond idealized theoretical models to address real-world experimental limitations.
